title: Batching + Quantization: Finance Calibration & Review Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is an internal review note for the Optimize team + Finance to align on how we calibrated the cost model changes driven by batching and 4-bit quantization recommendations. Draft intended for Finance sign-off before we bake new unit economics into pricing guidance and the cost-estimator in Console.

TL;DR (recommendation):
- Expect median per-token infra cost reduction of ~22% from combined batching + quantization (conservative baseline).
- Target rollout: enable quantized variants for non-sensitive, latency-tolerant routes and apply batching policy suggestions in Dedicated autoscaler for throughput-heavy customers.
- Finance approval needed on: (1) use of profiler run samples vs. billing-derived unit costs for baseline; (2) risk allowance for quality-related re-gen costs.

Key levers considered:
- Batching (dynamic continual batching): reduces per-token kernel overhead; impact highly dependent on request concurrency and latency SLO.
- Quantization (4-bit QAT / PTQ hybrid): lowers GPU memory and may improve throughput on Ampere/Instinct depending on kernel coverage.
- KV cache / prefix caching: reduces repeated compute for multi-turn chat; modeled separately but included in sensitivity sweep.

Data sources & provenance (notes on quality):
1) Billing exports (GCP/AWS invoice month windows): used for top-level $/GPU-hour and total infra spend by cluster. Caveat: includes non-inference infra overhead (monitoring, storage).
2) Console invocation logs (Jan 2025 - Oct 2025): request counts, latency buckets, route tags. Used to derive request size distribution and concurrency profiles. Sampling bias: older beta customers overrepresented.
3) Profiler runs (internal perf-benchmarks/2025): microbench runs per model variant (int8/4-bit/fp16), with sequence-length sweep. These runs give per-token GPU-time estimates under controlled load; important for kernel-specific speedups.
4) SRE telemetry (GPU utilization traces + preemption rates): used for utilization-to-cost mapping in Dedicated pools.
5) Customer POCs (three customers shared detailed traces): used to validate end-to-end impact on real workloads.

Which source is canonical for what: billing exports = canonical for total spend; profiler runs = canonical for relative perf deltas; console logs = canonical for request mix. We explicitly do NOT use profiler absolute latency as direct billable time (needs mapping via utilization model).

Calibration methodology (two-step):
A) Offline sim: combine profiler-derived per-token GPU-seconds with observed request mixes to simulate token-hours, then apply billing €/GPU-hour to estimate infra $/token. We include GPU-utilization overhead factor (1.18) to account for packing/idle time observed in SRE traces.
B) Runtime A/B: small-scale Dedicated and Hosted A/B (heat-up period 7 days) to measure delta in real infra spend after turning on config. This is the final tie-breaker for finance sign-off.

Assumptions encoded in the model (explicit):
- Baseline model variant = fp16 with continuous batching disabled (current default for hosted).
- Batching speedup curve = piecewise linear derived from profiler: 1.0x at concurrency=1, 1.45x at concurrency=8, 1.8x at concurrency=24 (seq len 256). We conservatively scale these by -10% for hosted workloads due to variable arrival patterns.
- Quantization delta = measured median 1.25x throughput improvement for 4-bit on Ampere in our profiler; apply 0.9x adjustment for real-world memory-bound routes.
- Re-gen overhead for quality delta: assume 0.5% increase in downstream token re-generation for routes flagged "sensitive to quant" (applies to 12% of routes). This maps to additional cost and a quality penalty bucket.
- Utilization multiplier = 1.18 (from SRE) for Dedicated packing inefficiencies; Hosted uses 1.06 multiplier.

Sample numeric snapshot (conservative baseline):
- Baseline infra $/1k tokens (fp16, no batching) = $0.0152
- After batching only (median arrival mix) = $0.0119 (-21.7%)
- After batching + 4-bit quant = $0.0094 (-38.2% vs baseline, -21% vs batching-only)
Notes: these are model outputs from the "1A2b3cBatchQuantizationCostModel" sheet (linked above).

Sensitivity analysis (high level):
- Best case: high concurrency + stable request sizes -> up to -45% per-token cost.
- Worst case: low concurrency + quality-induced re-gen -> as low as -5% net improvement or slight regression for select routes.
- Key sensitivities: concurrency distribution, fraction of latency-sensitive requests, actual quantization kernel availability per platform.

Finance sign-off checklist (what Finance should validate):
- [ ] Confirm we can use profiler-relative deltas mapped through utilization multipliers rather than requiring full end-to-end billing-only proof for all recommendations.
- [ ] Confirm the risk allowance / contingency percentage for model-quality re-gen (we propose 3% of infra savings be held as buffer in forecasting for Q1 rollout).
- [ ] Approve staging plan for pricing guidance change (we propose soft-launch for non-enterprise hosted customers; enterprise customers will be notified and given an opt-in window).
- [ ] Validate mapping of cloud discounts/reserved instances into unit-cost (current model uses blended $/GPU-hour from billing exports; Finance may prefer net-of-reservations view).

Operational rollout & guardrails:
- Start: Enable quantized variants as opt-in image for internal routes and POC customers for 2 weeks.
- Observability: add per-route quality regression monitors (prompt-based tests) and an infra delta dashboard with actual spend by route.
- Kill-switch: auto-fallback to fp16 if quality regressions cross threshold or latency SLO violations >2%.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Kernel availability on certain hardware -> Mitigation: fall back to fp16 or int8 variants; route-aware kernel mapping in deployment graph.
- Risk: Underestimated re-gen cost -> Mitigation: A/B with 100 customer-days before budget changes; hold 3% contingency.
- Risk: Finance prefers invoice-level proof -> Mitigation: schedule cross-team sync with Finance (INF-2345, FIN-678) and propose a small paid pilot where we shift BQs to quantized images for a handful of paying customers.

Open questions (need decisions):
1) Final contingency buffer percentage for finance forecasting (we propose 3%).
2) Which customer tiers are allowed for immediate auto-opt (hosted free-tier only vs. paid small customers).
3) Do we include an explicit line in pricing to call out "quantized variant" discounts, or keep savings as internal efficiency to protect margin?

Action items & owners (short):
- Priya: schedule Finance deep-dive (target week of 2026-02-22) and prepare one-slide summary for execs.
- Alex: run additional profiler sweeps for seq-len 64 and 512 (due 2026-02-01) to fill gaps in sensitivity table.
- Riley: wire up infra-delta dashboard prototype and per-route spend view (due 2026-02-10).
- Samir: draft A/B test plan and risk rollback triggers (due 2026-02-05).

Meeting notes snippet (2026-02-12 sync):
- Finance asked for clarity on how reserved-instance coverage affects blended $/GPU-hour (we currently blend; Finance prefers separated view).
- SRE asked that we avoid immediate global flip for Dedicated pools — recommend per-cluster opt-in and a 48-hour warmup window.
- Product ops requested that we auto-tag routes that are chatty (candidate for caching) so we can prioritize batching recommendations.

Appendix / references:
- Perf sheets: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1A2b3cBatchQuantizationCostModel (main workbook)
- A/B plan draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345
- Finance request ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-678
- Confluence: Batching + Quantization Playbook (link above)

Quick note about tone: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and conservative. It documents assumptions so Finance can push back on any that look optimistic. Please add comments inline in the spreadsheet for specific rows that Finance wants reworked.

-- end --
